These are research questions; no project results are asserted here.</p><h2>Oceanographic conditions</h2><p>Coordinated sampling and environmental observations provide the context for examining associations between marine microbiome responses and changing ocean conditions. Sampling comparisons will account for seasonality, local conditions and geographical differences in exposure to ENSO.</p><h2>Functional potential and selected microbial groups</h2><p>Metagenomic sequencing examines microbial functional and nutrient-cycling potential. Targeted studies of selected groups, including resident and introduced <i>Vibrio</i> lineages and potentially pathogenic strains, complement this community-wide perspective. Gene abundance alone does not establish activity or an ecosystem process rate.</p><h2>From questions to observations</h2><p>The <a href="about.html">Project page</a> describes the study design and molecular approach. The <a href="protocol.html">sampling protocol</a> sets out collection and tracking procedures.</p><h2>Interpretation and data release</h2><p>Detection of a potentially pathogenic lineage does not by itself establish viability, disease occurrence or health risk. Scientific datasets will be published only after review and authorization by the contributing partners.</p></section></div><footer class="site-footer"><div><strong>GLOBE</strong><p>Marine microbiome research.<br>Independent international scientific collaboration.</p></div><p>Project scope: 30 coastal stations · 23 countries<br><a href="../pages/news.html">News</a> · <a href="../pages/resources.html">Sources & resources</a> · <a href="../pages/protocol.html">Sampling protocol</a> · <a href="../pages/privacy.html">Privacy & data use</a> · <a href="../pages/members.html">Partner workspace</a><br>Independent international scientific collaboration</p></footer><script src="../assets/js/site.js?v=20261122-continuous"></script>
